message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I was in the right or wrong for locking my roommate and her friend out of our dorm room. Let me start by understanding the situation better. We live in a dorm room with two beds and desks, pretty standard. My roommate and her friend have started doing something that's really annoying. Whenever my boyfriend and I are in our room, and they leave, they leave the door wide open. They laugh and say "this is what you get" as if it's for showing minimal PDA (public display of affection) with my boyfriend in my room. But my boyfriend and I aren't doing anything, we're usually just watching Netflix in my bed. I feel like this is an invasion of my privacy. People in the dorm walk the halls, and I'm uncomfortable with that, especially since they're doing it intentionally to make me feel that way. Tonight, they left the room giggling and said "good luck" as they left the door open. They do this going in and out of the room like five times an hour. Each time I get up and close the door... I get sick of it on their like sixth trip, so I just lock the door. I know she has the key, but if I have to go through the hassle of getting up to close the door, they can go through the hassle of unlocking it. Anyway, the friend comes for their seventh trip and can't open the door and starts banging like crazy. I don't open the door because she knew what she was doing. She went back wherever she and my roommate were hanging and got the key and came in. She then told me it was very rude that I locked the door because "it's my roommate's room." I calmly said if you're going to make me get up and close the door, you can go through the process of unlocking it. My boyfriend also asked why they were acting so passive-aggressive for no reason. She laughed and called me disrespectful again and left, leaving the door wide open. Am I really the asshole for just wanting my door kept closed so everyone passing by doesn't see me in my bed? Alright, so I need to figure out if I was right or wrong in this situation. Let's break it down. First, the issue is about privacy. I feel that my roommate and her friend are intentionally leaving the door open to invade my privacy when my boyfriend and I are in the room. They find it amusing, but I find it intrusive. I tried to handle it by closing the door each time they left, but that got frustrating after multiple times. So, I decided to lock the door to prevent them from entering without unlocking it. They reacted by banging on the door and later called me disrespectful. Now, I need to assess whether my actions were justified or not. On one hand, I have a right to privacy in my own room, especially when I'm with my boyfriend. It's reasonable to expect that the door can be closed to maintain that privacy. My roommate and her friend's behavior seems to be intentionally disruptive and invasive. On the other hand, it's a shared space. The room is technically my roommate's room, so she might feel that she has the right to access it whenever she wants. By locking the door, I might be overstepping, especially if I don't have exclusive rights to the room. But wait, it's a dorm room with two beds. I assume both of us have equal rights to the room. So, if I'm in my bed with my boyfriend, and they're in their bed, we should both have the right to privacy. However, the problem arises when they keep leaving the door open, which seems like a deliberate action to make me uncomfortable. They're not just forgetting to close the door; they're doing it intentionally to mock me. So, by locking the door, I'm trying to assert my right to privacy. But by doing so, I'm also restricting their access to the room, which might be seen as rude or possessive. I think the key here is communication. Instead of locking the door, maybe I should have talked to my roommate about how their actions are making me uncomfortable. That way, we could find a solution that respects both of our needs. But in the heat of the moment, I locked the door, which led to conflict. So, perhaps my initial reaction was impulsive and not the best approach. In conclusion, while I have a right to privacy, locking the door without discussing it first might have been the wrong approach. It's better to address the issue calmly and find a mutual solution rather than taking matters into my own hands.
